Package com.github.crittscott.somestacks.gametest

Class StoragePileChecks

java.lang.Object
com.github.crittscott.somestacks.gametest.StoragePileChecks
public final class StoragePileChecks extends Object
Storage pile behavior in a live level that does not touch loader-native automation directly: deposits filling partial stacks before empty ones, growth when a pile fills, and settling consolidating, packing, and sorting. Capability/Transfer-API-facing tests stay in each loader's own StoragePileGameTests.

  • Method Details

    • depositFillsCompatiblePartialBeforeEmptySlot

      public static void depositFillsCompatiblePartialBeforeEmptySlot(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      A deposit fills a compatible partial stack before using an empty slot. To reproduce in-game: leave a partial stack of one item in Storage, then deposit more of that item. The partial reaches its limit before any remainder appears in another cube.

    • fullPileGrowsByOneBlock

      public static void fullPileGrowsByOneBlock(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Depositing into a full Storage pile grows it upward by one block. To reproduce in-game: fill every slot in one Storage block, then deposit one more allowed item. A second Storage block appears above and holds the item.

    • settleConsolidatesExactIdentityAndPacksDown

      public static void settleConsolidatesExactIdentityAndPacksDown(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Settlement merges only exact component identities, restores legal stack sizes, sorts, and packs downward. To reproduce in-game: put scattered compatible and component-distinct items in a Storage pile through automation, then let it settle. Compatible items merge at the base while distinct component or damage variants remain separate in stable order.

    • extractionSettlesOnScheduledBlockTick

      public static void extractionSettlesOnScheduledBlockTick(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Extraction schedules settlement instead of leaving a lasting gap. To reproduce in-game: store two different stacks, extract the lower visible stack, and wait a moment. The remaining stack packs into the first Storage position.

    • emptyTemporaryPileDisappearsButPermanentPileRemains

      public static void emptyTemporaryPileDisappearsButPermanentPileRemains(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Empty temporary piles disappear while permanent piles retain their blocks. To reproduce in-game: empty one ordinary Storage pile, then toggle another permanent with an empty hand in permanence mode and empty it. Only the permanent block remains.

    • comparatorReadsTheWholePileFromEveryBlock

      public static void comparatorReadsTheWholePileFromEveryBlock(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Every block in a Storage pile reports the same whole-pile comparator signal. To reproduce in-game: make a two-block pile with contents only in one block and place comparators against both blocks. Their outputs match.

    • ordinaryPlacementBelowPermanentPileRepairsDerivedState

      public static void ordinaryPlacementBelowPermanentPileRepairsDerivedState(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Placing Storage beneath a permanent pile preserves permanence, repacks contents into the new base, and republishes comparator output. To reproduce in-game: make a full one-block permanent pile with a comparator, place another Storage block beneath it, and wait. The joined pile stays permanent, moves contents downward, and the comparator changes to the two-block fill value.

    • breakingMiddleBlockDropsItsContentsAndSplitsThePile

      public static void breakingMiddleBlockDropsItsContentsAndSplitsThePile(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Breaking the middle Storage block drops only that block's contents and leaves independent runs above and below. To reproduce in-game: put different items in each block of a three-block pile and break the middle block. Its items drop, while the other two blocks keep their own contents and settle independently.

    • comparatorReservesZeroForAnEmptyPile

      public static void comparatorReservesZeroForAnEmptyPile(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      The comparator range reserves 0 for an empty pile, as a vanilla container's does. A pile is large enough that a proportional conversion would round hundreds of items down to 0, so the reserved value is what makes an emptiness circuit read a pile correctly.

      To reproduce in-game: compare an empty Storage pile, the same pile with one item, and a full pile. Their comparator outputs are 0, at least 1, and 15 respectively.

    • comparatorContributionLoadsAndTracksMutations

      public static void comparatorContributionLoadsAndTracksMutations(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      To reproduce in-game: fill a Storage pile with mixed stack limits, save and reopen the world, then extract an item. Comparators match the contents immediately after loading and again after extraction, before the deferred settlement runs.
